jurisdiction.publisher: Health Canada - MedEffect Canada / Canada Vigilance Program

domain: pharmacovigilance - adverse drug reaction reports (Canada Vigilance database)
prediction_question: Hypothetical task this source would support (parked): predict the outcome or seriousness of a reported adverse drug reaction (patient demographics, suspect drug, reaction) from the Canada Vigilance reports - the Canadian counterpart of FAERS/openFDA-style tasks.
prediction_time: Would be the report's receipt by the Canada Vigilance Program; seriousness/outcome classification is assigned and updated later, so timing would be stateable - but the source never got that far (access blocker below).
target_definition: Not fixed: report-level seriousness or outcome class. Moot given the park reason.

sources.name: Canada Vigilance Adverse Reaction Online Database (open.canada.ca packages 9cbaef00 / 98cad9a3)
sources.api: NONE - measured 2026-10-21 via anonymous CKAN package_show: both packages list ONLY HTML resources (the English and French database pages); no CSV, API or bulk resource exists on the records. The database itself is an interactive query form (search by drug, reaction, date range, with on-screen results).
sources.license: open.canada.ca records carry license_id ca-ogl-lgo (Open Government Licence - Canada 2.0); but licence on viewable database content does not create a bulk channel.
sources.access: measured 2026-10-21: CKAN package_show for 98cad9a3 answered anonymously (resources: 2 HTML links). Direct fetch of the database page from this coordinator timed out twice (90 s read timeout, two attempts on 2026-10-21) - recorded as coordinator-side network behaviour; the CKAN record itself is the evidence for the resource shape, so the access verdict does not rest on the page fetch.

sources.name: 'Data on cannabis adverse reactions' (open.canada.ca package 371d84b2) - checked as a possible bulk side-channel
sources.api: measured 2026-10-21 via CKAN package_show: resources are PDF annual reports only (rept_ocss-2020 through 2024-annual-report.pdf, English and French) - the 'data' package is a set of PDF reports, not machine-readable data.
sources.access: CKAN package_show anonymous; resource list read back (12 PDF resources, no CSV/API).

license_evidence.note: open.canada.ca records list license_id ca-ogl-lgo for the Canada Vigilance packages (measured 2026-10-21). Licence is not the blocker; there is no machine-readable redistribution channel to license in the first place.

split_strategy: Not built - no bulk access to measure a panel from. The query-form database returns on-screen results only; a panel would have to be assembled by scripted query traffic, which is exactly the kind of undocumented scraping the pipeline avoids as provenance.

measurements.access_probe_2026_10_21: CKAN package_show x3 (two Vigilance packages, one cannabis-ADR package): all resources are HTML (query-form pages) or PDF (annual reports). No CSV, no API, no bulk export on any of the three records. Database landing page: two fetch attempts timed out from the coordinator (90 s), recorded. Total probe cost: 3 small API calls + 2 failed page fetches.
measurements.task_family_comparison: Even with access, differentiation would be uphill: the US counterpart (FDA FAERS via openFDA) ships event-level ADR data through a documented anonymous API and already exists in this bench's family (openfda-food-recall-classification is the recalls sibling; ADR-outcome prediction on FAERS is a heavily published literature). A Canadian ADR task's novelty would rest on the Canadian-only reporting population and the seriousness/outcome coding - a thin contribution against the public FAERS ecosystem.

rejection_reason: PARKED on access: the Canada Vigilance adverse reaction data has no bulk or API channel - the open.canada.ca records list HTML query-form resources only, and the related 'data on cannabis adverse reactions' package is PDF annual reports (a PDF-only publisher is a park, not a go). Assembling a panel would require undocumented scripted scraping of an interactive form, which this pipeline does not treat as acceptable provenance. Secondary reason: even unparked, the FAERS/openFDA ecosystem already serves the ADR-outcome task family publicly.
next_action: Parked. Unpark only if Health Canada publishes a machine-readable export of Canada Vigilance (watch the two open.canada.ca packages for a CSV/API resource appearing, e.g. on the next Canada tick), or the operator records a risk acceptance that a browser-captured query export is acceptable provenance - the UNHCR precedent (unhcr-refugee-data-finder) applies verbatim here.
